chunks: Abu Dawood, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from 'Amr ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is it permissible for a man to speak during the Adhan?' He said, 'There is no problem.' I said, 'During the Iqamah?' He said, 'No.'

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةِ: Iqamah (the second call to prayer, signaling the start)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to speak during the Adhan and Iqamah?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the permissibility of casual speech during the Adhan while maintaining its prohibition during the Iqamah, reflecting the distinct ritual statuses of the two calls. This distinction highlights the scholarly view that the Iqamah, being immediately preceding the prayer's commencement, requires greater solemnity and attentiveness than the initial Adhan. The ruling underscores the importance of preserving the spiritual atmosphere of the call to prayer in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Abu Dawood, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat, from Al Husayn Bin Usman, from Amro Bin Nasr who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘Can the man speak during the Azān?’ Heasws said: ‘No problem’. I said, ‘During the Iqamah?’ Heasws said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 10. Abu Dawud has narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from al-Husayn ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Amr ibn abu Nasr who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, “Can a man speak during Adhan?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’ I then asked, about ‘Iqamah. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it is not acceptable.’”
